equation.name: How hot a star's surface shines

source.text: Carroll, B. W. and Ostlie, D. A. 2017, An Introduction to Modern Astrophysics, 2nd edn, Cambridge University Press

explain.curious: How hot a star's surface is follows from how much light leaves how much surface.
explain.science: Effective temperature is the temperature of a black body with the star's radius and luminosity. It defines the surface temperature rather than measuring it.

references: Hansen, C. J., Kawaler, S. D. and Trimble, V. 2004, Stellar Interiors, 2nd edn, Springer, section 1.4 (main-sequence lifetime scaling). doi:10.1007/978-1-4419-9110-2

equation.name: How long a star burns hydrogen

source.text: Hansen, C. J., Kawaler, S. D. and Trimble, V. 2004, Stellar Interiors, 2nd edn, Springer

explain.curious: A star lives on its fuel divided by how fast it burns it. Bright heavy stars burn out in millions of years; dim red dwarfs outlast the present age of the universe.
explain.science: The usable hydrogen scales with mass and the burn rate with luminosity, so the lifetime scales as M/L, normalised to the Sun's 10 Gyr. Ignores the larger burnt fraction in fully convective dwarfs and mass loss in massive stars.
